dublinCore.title: Impulse and Frequency Response Analyzer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Signals and Systems
Impulse Response
Step Response
Frequency Response
LTI Systems
dublinCore.description: Shows the impulse response, step response, magnitude response and phase response of five LTI systems (Butterworth low-pass and high-pass filters, differentiator, integrator and second-order resonant system) side by side, with linked cursors and sliders for cutoff frequency, filter order and damping ratio.

learningObjectives: Explain why the impulse response completely characterizes an LTI system
Relate the step response to the impulse response through integration
Connect features of h(t) (decay rate, ringing) to features of H(f) (cutoff, resonant peak)
Compare how low-pass, high-pass, differentiating, integrating and resonant systems change a signal in time and in frequency
Predict the response to a pulse or a square wave by superposing shifted step responses
prerequisites: Unit impulse and unit step functions
Convolution and the meaning of an impulse response
Complex numbers, magnitude and phase, and decibels

misconceptions.misconception: The impulse response and the frequency response describe different aspects of a system
misconceptions.correction: They are the same system seen in two domains; each determines the other through the Fourier transform
misconceptions.evidence: Move the cutoff slider and watch h(t) and |H(f)| change together

misconceptions.misconception: A higher filter order only changes the frequency response
misconceptions.correction: A sharper cutoff brings overshoot, ringing and more delay in the time domain
misconceptions.evidence: Step the order from 1 to 4 and watch s(t) overshoot by 0%, 4%, 8% and 11%

misconceptions.misconception: A system with a wide bandwidth responds slowly
misconceptions.correction: Rise time is about 0.35/fc for a first-order filter, so wider bandwidth means a faster response
misconceptions.evidence: Raise the cutoff from 1 Hz to 4 Hz and watch h(t) narrow and s(t) rise faster

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Four plots for a selected linear time-invariant system: impulse response and step response against time, and magnitude in decibels and phase in degrees against frequency. Menus choose the system and the input signal, and sliders set the cutoff frequency, filter order and damping ratio.

responsiveBreakpoints.description: Below 600 px the fonts shrink and long plot captions and axis labels switch to short forms

controls.label: System
controls.description: Chooses the LTI system: Butterworth low-pass, Butterworth high-pass, differentiator, integrator or second-order resonant system

controls.label: Input
controls.description: Chooses the input signal: unit step, 0.5 s rectangular pulse or 1 Hz square wave

controls.label: Cutoff fc / unity-gain f0 / natural fn
controls.description: Sets the cutoff frequency of a filter, the unity-gain frequency of the differentiator and integrator, or the natural frequency of the resonant system

controls.label: Filter order N
controls.description: Sets the order of the Butterworth filter; greyed out for the other systems

controls.label: Damping ratio
controls.description: Sets the damping ratio of the resonant system; greyed out for the other systems

controls.label: Export h(t) as CSV
controls.description: Downloads the regular part of h(t) and s(t) sampled every 0.01 s from 0 to 2.5 s

visualElements.description: Impulse response h(t) with arrows for impulses and doublets
Step response s(t), or the output y(t) for a pulse or square-wave input, with the input drawn in grey
Magnitude of H(f) in decibels on a logarithmic frequency axis, with the cutoff marker and a frequency cursor
Phase of H(f) in degrees on a logarithmic frequency axis, with the cutoff marker and a frequency cursor

model.description: Closed-form impulse, step and frequency responses of five LTI systems; pulse and square-wave outputs are sums of shifted step responses
equations: s(t) = integral of h from -infinity to t
H(f) = integral of h(t) exp(-j 2 pi f t) dt
Resonant: H(s) = wn^2 / (s^2 + 2 zeta wn s + wn^2)
assumptions: All responses are closed-form; impulses and doublets are drawn as arrows
Pulse and square-wave outputs are built by superposing shifted step responses
limitations: Only continuous-time systems, one input at a time
Time axis is fixed at -0.25 s to 2.5 s and frequency axis at 0.1 Hz to 100 Hz

instructionalStrategies: Linked multiple representations of one system
Compare systems by changing one slider at a time
extensions: Add a band-pass or notch system
Show the output spectrum for the square-wave input
